_comment: Drift detector parameters. Config, never constants — the same discipline
as the review threshold and the SLA: changing how sensitive detection is
must not be a code change.
baseline_n: documents of stable operation that define the baseline. Below
this the detector reports 'baseline' and makes NO drift claims — the
cold-start guard. 50 is enough for a usable std on a rate around a few
percent and small enough that a new tenant is protected within a day.
z_threshold: standard deviations from the baseline mean before a document
counts as a breach. 3.0 is ~0.1% of a normal tail per signal per
document; with 3 signals that is a false breach every ~110 documents,
which is why breaches alone do not raise drift.
consecutive_k: consecutive breaching documents on ONE signal before drift
is declared. This is what separates a weird document from a changed
format. At k=3 the chance of a false flag is (0.001)^3 per signal —
once in ~330 million documents — while a genuine format change breaches
every document and is caught in 3.
min_std: floor on the baseline standard deviation, so a signal that never
varied in the baseline cannot produce an infinite z-score. Rate signals
use a Laplace-smoothed Bernoulli sigma instead and ignore this.
profile_dim: buckets in the hashed text profile. 64 was measurably too few:
a page of invoice text has hundreds of distinct tokens, so at 64 buckets
the collisions smear every document toward every other one. Measured on
a redesigned-vs-normal comparison, the drifted z-score mean went 2.08 at
dim 64 to 3.17 at dim 1024. Above ~1024 the gain flattens and the stored
centroid gets large for no benefit. One centroid per tenant x doc type,
so the storage cost is a few tens of KB in total.
